evidence_policy: Every number is parsed from the logs of this run. Wall time is diagnostic_only on this shared host; bit identity, work counters, allocation counts and user-space instruction counts are primary.

bit_identity.compared: attempts, accepted and rejected steps, Jacobian reuses, internal and clipped steps, the whole WorkCounters, every output time and state, every accepted (t, y) (Jacobian-callback trace of both drivers and the client driver's accept control), all as f64 bits

off_policy_faer.note: The faer mode on problems where the protected policy picks the in-place LU: a valid solver, not a bit-identical one.

allocations.counter: process-global counting allocator, one test in its own binary

wall_diagnostic.note: Seven interleaved repetitions per case, arm order rotating; each repetition is the mean of runs_per_repetition runs. The host is shared and loaded (see loadavg): these ratios are not a verdict.

instruction_counts.counter: perf stat -e instructions:u (user space, child threads included)

verdicts.zero_allocations_per_step_faer: NOT_MET_BY_DESIGN: every faer factorization allocates inside LuFactorization::new, in the protected driver as well; see allocations.faer_rows_reported_not_asserted

notes: Faer identity is shown on the mean-field Brusselator (n = 200, half-full Jacobian): the protected policy picks faer only above order 64 with more than 10 % nonzeros, which Robertson, HIRES and the banded 1D Brusselator (N = 32, N = 100) never reach. On those the protected LU is in place; the faer client there is reported under off_policy_faer.
Accepted states are compared through a recording Jacobian callback (one call per accepted state in either driver) and, for the client driver, through its accept control.

exploratory/02 was run with a pre-commit variant of the faer factorization that dropped the old factors before building the new ones; the committed code builds first, as the protected driver does. Every exploratory wall ratio was taken on a loaded host and is not evidence for or against that variant.
The faer path takes thousands of minor page faults per run in both drivers (wall_diagnostic.rows[*].*_minor_page_faults_per_run); the cause was not investigated in this node.

TimedStageClient times the three trait phases only. RHS evaluations and the stage vector work belong to the driver, so the phases do not sum to the wall time (wall_diagnostic.summary[*].timed_phases_over_wall).
